pr.title: coverage: Never emit improperly-ordered coverage regions
pr.description:
If we emit a coverage region that is improperly ordered (end < start), `llvm-cov` will fail with `coveragemap_error::malformed`, which is inconvenient for users and also very hard to debug.

Ideally we would fix the root causes of these situations, but they tend to occur in very obscure edge-case scenarios (often involving nested macros), and we don't always have a good MCVE to work from. So it makes sense to also have a catch-all check that will prevent improperly-ordered regions from ever being emitted.

---

This is mainly aimed at resolving #119453. We don't have a specific way to reproduce it, which is why I haven't been able to add a test case in this PR. But based on the information provided in that issue, this change seems likely to avoid the error in `llvm-cov`.

@rustbot label +A-code-coverage
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage historically emitted coverage code regions without validating their coordinates, so a region could be improperly ordered (end < start), contain a 0 coordinate, or have the high bit set in end_col. llvm-cov treats such regions as malformed and exits fatally. The fix adds a catch-all `check_code_region` filter that discards any region failing those invariants (and debug-asserts), rather than fixing each root cause in nested-macro edge cases.
analysis.originalLogic: In `make_code_region`, after doctest offsetting, the code built a region and returned it unconditionally: `Some(CodeRegion { file_name, start_line: start_line as u32, start_col: start_col as u32, end_line: ..., end_col: ... })`. There was no validation of ordering, zero coordinates, or the end_col high bit before emitting the region.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Returning every constructed CodeRegion as-is (historical behavior) can emit a region that is improperly ordered (end < start), has any 1-based line/column coordinate equal to 0, or has the high bit of end_col set. Emitting such a region makes llvm-cov exit with a fatal `coveragemap_error::malformed` error. The corrected behavior routes the region through `check_code_region`, which returns `Some(region)` only when `all_nonzero && end_col_has_high_bit_unset && is_ordered`; otherwise it logs/debug-asserts and returns `None` (discarding the region).
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions/methods/closures eligible for coverage instrumentation (constants excluded), compiled with coverage enabled, especially source containing obscure nested-macro edge cases and doctests where source-map line/column spans may be reversed or degenerate. Coordinates are expected to be 1-based and the end_col high bit reserved for gap regions.
analysis.trigger: A coverage-eligible function produces a CodeRegion whose (start_line,start_col) is greater than (end_line,end_col), or any coordinate is 0, or end_col has bit 31 set — commonly arising from obscure nested-macro expansions or doctest offsetting.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled for a function/method/closure (constants are not eligible).
A source span is converted into a code region via make_code_region, including doctest offsetting and 1-based coordinate adjustment.
The resulting region violates one of: all coordinates nonzero, end_col high bit unset, or (start <= end).
pitfalls: Do not attempt to fix individual macro-expansion root causes; this change is a defensive catch-all that drops bad regions.
The end_col high bit is reserved to mark gap regions, so it must be unset for normal code regions.
Coordinates are supposed to be 1-based; a 0 coordinate may be misinterpreted by llvm-cov and must be rejected.
Comparison must be on the tuple (start_line,start_col) <= (end_line,end_col), not lines alone.
Debug builds ICE via debug_assert on a rejected region, while release builds log and discard; a test must not assume rejection always panics.
No MCVE or regression test was added in this PR, so do not claim a specific reproduction was exercised.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two programs differing only in whether a coverage-eligible region is valid: one that yields a well-ordered 1-based region and one engineered/edge-case source (e.g. nested macros or doctest-offset spans) that would produce an out-of-order, zero-coordinate, or high-bit end_col region. Compile with coverage enabled, then inspect/consume the emitted coverage map with llvm-cov. Corrected behavior: malformed regions are dropped so llvm-cov does not report `coveragemap_error::malformed`; historical behavior emits the bad region and can trigger that fatal error. Since the PR added no regression test and had no reproduction, avoid asserting a concrete MCVE; verify at the coverage-mapping/llvm-cov boundary rather than claiming runtime execution.
